parts.note: not the phone call made at the receiver's expense: in battle, troops who strike back at an advancing enemy turn its charge round

explanation.surface: A caller asks the operator to make the call collect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reverse the charge' is a stock telephone phrase; read literally it means meeting a charge with one of your own.
explanation.definitionFit: A military response that turns an enemy's assault back on it reverses that charge.

definitions.meaning: a loose coat or boiler suit worn over clothes

explanation.surface: A general appears wearing a protective coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like an army officer; it is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means taken as a whole and also names a coverall worn to protect clothing.

clue.text: Boy is right to keep up

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to retain someone's property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A boy is told he is entitled to keep something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right to keep' reads as a pair of words but together they define a lien, which 'up' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Neil is a common male first name, so it can stand for a lad.

clue.text: Defile and glen in the country

indicators.note: to defile is to corrupt or spoil, so the letters of and glen are messed up

explanation.surface: A mountain pass and a valley out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defile' looks like a noun for a narrow pass, matching 'glen'; it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: England is one of the nations of the United Kingdom, a country.

clue.text: Chasing a double century, I will have hit all round — to get this?

definitions.text: Chasing a double century, I will have hit all round — to get this?

indicators.note: the later pieces follow on after the first ones
doubling the century letter gives two hundred, as in a cricketer's double ton

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: the beating word goes round the letter I

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or beat

explanation.surface: A cricketer chasing two hundred hits all round the ground, hoping for praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chasing' puts the hit-and-I piece after the rest; the whole clue also describes the batsman's reward, in cricket a double century being two hundred runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A batsman scoring a double century would earn loud public praise, which is the applause named.

parts.note: read two ways: not wild, as a domesticated animal is, and dull, not thrilling

explanation.surface: A lukewarm verdict on something rather dull.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase hints both at a domesticated creature and at something flat and uninspiring.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means domesticated rather than feral and also dull or uninspiring.

clue.text: Pick up as part of the service

definitions.meaning: a short prayer in a church service, said with the stress on the first syllable

explanation.surface: Someone picks up a part as part of a delivery service.
explanation.walkthrough: The church sense is stressed on the first syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means fetch or gather; the noun is a brief prayer in the Anglican liturgy.

clue.text: A chorister not involved in an arrangement

indicators.note: involved means tangled or complicated, so the letters of a chorister not are jumbled

explanation.surface: A choir member is left out of a musical arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not involved' looks like one idea; 'involved' alone is the signal and 'not' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoring music for the instruments of a band or ensemble is the arranging of it.

clue.text: How to make a speedy apology?

definitions.text: How to make a speedy apology?

parts.words: How to make a speedy apology?
parts.note: express reads as fast, like an express train, but the phrase means to voice one's sorrow

explanation.surface: A question about apologising quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: The first word of the phrase means to put into words, not rapid.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying sorry is voicing remorse, and the first word doubles as fast.

clue.text: Dazed American general in retreat, and encircled

indicators.note: the turned name sits within the word for encircled

parts.note: something encircled has a ring round it; ring is taken as the encircling word

indicators.note: a general in retreat goes backwards, so his name is read from the end

parts.note: Robert E. Lee, the Confederate general of the American Civil War

explanation.surface: A defeated American general falls back, surrounded and stunned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retreat' reads as one phrase, but 'retreat' alone turns the general backwards and 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reeling is staggering, their head spinning, so stunned or dazed is a synonym.

definitions.meaning: an obsession or fixation, as in an inferiority one named by Freudians

explanation.surface: A psychologist describes an intricate mental condition.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both intricate and, in psychology, a group of repressed feelings shaping behaviour.

definitions.meaning: a judge tries a case, that is listens to it in court
to attend to sounds with the ears

explanation.surface: An exasperated plea for someone to pay attention.
explanation.definitionFit: A court trying a case is said to sit and take evidence on it; the word also simply means perceive sound.

clue.text: Old hat found in bar by a lake

parts.note: to bar something is to prohibit it
L is the standard abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned hat turns up in a pub beside a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old hat' is an idiom, not headgear.
explanation.definitionFit: Something old hat is stale and unoriginal, the same idea as trite or commonplace.

definitions.meaning: to gaze closely or squint at something
a person of the same rank or standing

explanation.surface: Someone searches for a match of equal standing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for peering closely and a noun for one's equal, as in a jury of one's fellows.

indicators.note: undoing the word Troy's takes its letters apart and rebuilds them

explanation.surface: A legend about the fall of Troy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undoing' reads as Troy's downfall; the 'S here counts as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative or account of events is a synonym for a tale.

clue.text: Three points going to my opponent

parts.note: east, north and east again are three compass points

explanation.surface: A rival scores three points against me.
explanation.walkthrough: 'points' are compass points, not a score.
explanation.definitionFit: A foe or adversary is one who opposes you, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Kissed perhaps — what starts usually between girl and boy

indicators.note: the picked letter goes in the middle of the two names

parts.note: Sal is a girl's name, short for Sally
Ted is a boy's name

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word usually is wanted

explanation.surface: A boy and girl usually greet with a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks the definition as an example: a kiss is one way to greet someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiss on the cheek is one form of greeting, so kissed is an instance of having greeted.

definitions.meaning: the written record of a meeting
sixty-second units, as in 'ten of these past four'

explanation.surface: Someone jots down what time it is.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a meeting's written record and a count of the small units of an hour.

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
to answer a purpose is to serve it or suffice

explanation.surface: A reader jots down an answer in a book's margin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'book' is a verb here, as in booking a table.
explanation.definitionFit: To book a seat or table is to set it aside in advance, a synonym.

clue.text: Sesame crackers one's fed to cat

indicators.note: the numeral is placed inside the scrambled letters
crackers means crazy, so the letters of sesame go wild

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Sesame biscuits are given to the cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crackers' looks like biscuits; it is the anagram signal on Sesame, and the numeral I goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Siamese is a slender blue-eyed breed of domestic cat.

clue.text: Model student allowed in gym after test

indicators.note: the gym piece comes after the test

parts.note: an exam is a test

indicators.note: the learner letter goes inside the gym letters

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school gym
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A model pupil is allowed into the gym after an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: L for learner is a British convention from the L-plate on learner drivers' cars.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern to copy or an ideal specimen is a model, as in setting a good one.

parts.note: current is electric current, not present-day policy: this instrument gauges the flow of electricity in amperes

explanation.surface: Something enables today's policies to happen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current measures' reads as present-day steps; here it is measuring electrical current.
explanation.definitionFit: The instrument named reads the strength of an electric flow, so it allows that quantity to be gauged.

clue.text: Don't vote and get a black mark

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a stain is a mark or blemish

explanation.surface: Refusing to vote earns you a black mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Declining to cast a ballot either way is to refrain, the formal word for it.

indicators.note: making the word new rearranges its letters

parts.note: Aintree is the Liverpool racecourse that hosts the Grand National

explanation.surface: A new apprentice jockey at Aintree, the British racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone learning a trade under supervision is a learner or apprentice.

indicators.note: the word for departing is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: to part is to go away or depart

explanation.surface: A driver turns round to leave in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: PART read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage of this name is a kind of vehicle.

indicators.note: only a stretch of letters within the phrase clergyman's estate is wanted

explanation.surface: A question about a vicar's property holdings.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'clergyman's estate'; the whole clue also defines, since a minister's house is part of his property.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish or Nonconformist minister's official house is a piece of church property he occupies.

indicators.note: the dance is without its nought

parts.note: the tango is an Argentine ballroom dance
O, a zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A dance performed without any taste or refinement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tastefulness' means full of taste, a strong flavour, not good taste.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp, distinctive flavour is a fullness of taste, which is what the word names.

indicators.note: the letters of a lot are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A singer has changed a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A singer with a low female or high male voice takes this vocal part.

parts.note: re means concerning or touching on
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An emotional article or pamphlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tract' reads as a pamphlet; it is an expanse of land.
explanation.definitionFit: An expanse or stretch of land is a region or zone of ground.

parts.note: over means in excess of, as in over fifty
a lap is one circuit of a track

explanation.surface: A runner covers part of more than one circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that partly extend over each other share some area, which is what the verb describes.

clue.text: Called in a long time back to put in order

indicators.note: the telephoning word goes inside
the word for a long period is read backwards

parts.note: an era is a long period of history
rang means telephoned, called

explanation.surface: Someone phoned in long ago to put things straight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the long period, giving ARE, and 'in' places the telephoning word between its second and third letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To set things out neatly or in sequence is to organise them, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Get the job and be accepted for a union

definitions.meaning: to be taken on or hired by an employer
to agree to marry, a union being a marriage

explanation.surface: A worker is hired and then admitted to a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' suggests a trade union; it is marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to be hired by an employer and to become betrothed.
